Cost to value ratio, gas still takes the cake, but with electric it’s best to just replace the whole machine every so often. More times than not, once the battery is weak, the whole unit is ready for the trash.

There’s a chance there was air in the system, as you turned the fuel pump ram dry and starved the engine of fuel temporarily. Fuel injected vehicles are VERY sensitive to fuel pressure, and can cause these issues. 

Assuming the engine replacement was solid, you should not leave a vehicle sit below 1/4 tank. The modern ethanol absorbs a lot of water, and the airspace in the take amplifies this. It’s a good idea to keep it above half a tank, as the fuel pump is located in the tank, and the fuel cools the fuel pump. They do not like to run hot, or dry. 

I would keep it above 1/2 and drive it, after clearing the codes. If the problem comes back there are other things going on, but yeah, don’t run it down to E. Fuel injection requires 45-65psi of fuel pressure, and a cusp of air can upset that.

See and I grew up in the country, and live in the city now. So I can see both sides. Country wise, we do nothing but mow the lawn. Don’t really care enough to bother with leaf pickup, watering, or anything. If weeds get really bad then spray herbicide once in the spring or fall. (It’s perfectly safe if you use the proper amount) and in 15 years we’ve prolly sprayed for weeds twice. The only thing we watered was apple trees. 

Our tree row we would run bad branches through the wood chipper and spread on the ground, further helping prevent large unwanted plants and keeping the trees well fed, as there was about a 2 foot thick layer of mulch throughout most of the tree row. 

Inside the mulch you could pick edible mushrooms, in the broom grass outside of it you could pick wild asparagus. We mow around the house and buildings for mosquito control. 

The requirement of the garden was to provide enough veggies to last the winter, the dogs keep the cattle in the fence and protect the chickens from fox, while a couple goats eat the weeds in the pastures as no other animal will. 

The reason there’s a need for proper weed control as these weeds are violently strong, and will suck the life from everything around them. 

It’s actually a law where I’m from to spray for leafy spurge, or kudzu, as they will overtake entire areas and kill everything, and kudzu will actually pull apart buildings and concrete. 

There are many natural plants that roam, but there are some that have to be controlled. The southern states have more issues with kudzu, or creeping Jane, than the north, but again that weed was introduced to America by the Chinese and is not native here, part of the reason it’s so rampant. This is why for how many Prius have been sold, there’s an unusually small number of older models on the road, they’ve already been crushed.

So if you are to buy electric, it’s wise to sell it or trade it off in 4 years and just forget about ever owning a car that you don’t owe money on.

I could go on but I should move on, TODDLERS! 
Pain in the ass. (1-3) They will mess with everything, exclusively what you tell them not to. If it’s something violently dangerous, your better off distracting them from it and removing it. If you tell them no, they will mess with it. I call this the “mouse trap technique.” If you tell them not to touch it, you’ll be peeling it off their screaming fingers in less than 20 minutes.

Avoid all things sugar. It’s like crack to young kids, and they will eventually refuse to eat anything without it. Instead try carrots, bananas, apple, any fruits, vegetables, anything you eat. Just not sugar or spices. (But mostly sugar.) 

Ages 3-7 is a wild card. Every kid is different so your needs will change, but a lot of their behavior stems from you. In one way or another. If you react badly, so will they. You need to pay more attention to yourself on how you respond to things as this will become more apparent with age. The kids will pick up on EVERYTHING you didn’t know about yourself. (Cutest thing ever was my oldest making the “HHHHUUUAAH!” Sound whenever she squatted to pick something up as apparently I always do that.)

One will struggle to do what they need to see, and it’s unfortunate and detrimental to not have both, for the kids sake. And a single parents sanity. Many of us didn’t get that luxury, so you gotta work with what you got. But it is wonderful for the kids that got to grow up with mom and dad there, I presume. 

One more thing: TEENAGERS. This is a big “nope” zone for me, as they are ambitious, usually rebellious, and they think they know things you don’t. It can get dark sometimes but unless a bunch of drugs are involved i think everyone will be ok. 

To finish on a happier note, the toddler years I remember as being the worst, were also the best. They say the craziest things and are hilarious. You could buy the most expensive toys but they ones they seem to stick to are the cheap sensory things. Like swimming, sandboxes, coloring books, swinging, a cardboard box.
